sentences.text: This dinosaur measured roughly four meters in length and weighed about 500 kilograms, making it one of the tiniest members of its group.
Unlike its famous relative, the back plates of this creature were more spike-shaped and covered less surface area.
A cluster of spikes on the tail end served as a defensive tool against predators.
Its mouth contained seven teeth at the front and between twenty-five and thirty further back.
Scientists note that the space inside its spine was unusually wide, possibly to hold a secondary brain center.
At a mass of 500 kilograms, this animal stands out as one of the smallest stegosaurians ever discovered.
Holes found within the back plates suggest they once carried blood vessels to help regulate body temperature.
These structures might have allowed the animal to change colors to warn enemies or attract partners.
Fossil hunters uncovered twelve separate individuals at the Dashanpu Quarry near Zigong in Sichuan province.
Dong Zhiming, Tang Zilu, and Zhou Shiwu formally named and described the genus in 1982.
The name combines an ancient title for Sichuan with a tribute to the poet Li Bai, known by the courtesy name Taibai.
Large spikes positioned above the hips likely helped defend against attacks coming from above.
Because the plates were smaller, they may not have been as good at controlling body heat as those of later species.
As one of the most primitive stegosaurians, it was placed in its own family called Huayangosauridae.
Its skull was broader and kept front teeth, a feature that disappeared in all later relatives.
Although it has its own family, it remains a basal member of the larger Stegosauria group.
This animal lived during the Bathonian to Callovian stages, roughly 165 million years ago, or between 170.9 and 154.8 million years ago.
Its environment included sauropods, the ornithopod Xiaosaurus, and the carnivorous theropod Gasosaurus.
Some researchers think specimen CV 721 might belong to a different species because of major differences.
Another idea proposes that males looked different from females, perhaps sporting horns on their heads.
A 2008 study by Mateus, Maidment, and Christiansen suggests Chungkingosaurus is closer to Huayangosaurus than to Stegosaurus.
